messages:
anna_support: FYI customer reported sudden 429 flood on their Dedicated pool this morning, says throughput dropped and console shows `x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0` on many requests. Tenant: t-acme-9, pool: dedicated-eu-west-1-prod. thread_ts=1837899999
mike_eng_infra: Got it. Do we have a sample req-id and headers from them? Any idea if they changed traffic shape?
anna_support: They attached a screenshot and a trace id: req_0a2b3c. They claim no traffic change. Console shows `x-rw-rate-limit-limit: 1000` but they expected higher.
jess_sre: Pulling enforcement metrics for dedicated-eu-west-1-prod now. I see spike of 429s starting ~2023-11-02T08:12Z, tenant-specific throttle count for t-acme-9 jumped sharply and stayed high ~40m. Current enforcement logs indicate unit=`requests_per_minute`.
ravi_product: Could be the classic unit mismatch we saw in the CLI import path. Support sometimes sets tokens/min but CSV/CLI can map to requests/min. If enforcement is counting requests, token-heavy workloads will hit limits fast.
mike_eng_infra: Paste the tenant quota blob from their bundle?
anna_support: From customer bundle:
```
tenant: t-acme-9
quota:
  limit: 1000
  unit: requests_per_minute
  burst: 50
```
They told us they intended `1000 tokens_per_minute`.
jess_sre: Confirmed in config history: last import replaced `tokens_per_minute` -> `requests_per_minute`. Enforcement treats `requests` and `tokens` differently; our admission mapping uses tokens for model families that consume many tokens per call. Their workload averages ~400 tokens/request per logs.
mike_eng_infra: Enforcement sample: 
```
[rate-limiter] tenant=t-acme-9 enforced_limit=1000 unit=requests_per_minute remaining=0
[rate-limiter] req=req_0a2b3c tokens=421
```
So one request equals 421 tokens; under requests/min config they're limited severely.
ravi_product: Immediate mitigation options: 1) change tenant unit back to `tokens_per_minute`; 2) temporarily increase requests cap; 3) apply a tenant-specific rule to bypass strict request counting for known token-heavy model families. Thoughts?
jess_sre: Fastest safe step: change unit to `tokens_per_minute` and set quota to `100000` tokens/min while we validate. Also add small cap bump if customer requests quick relief. I'll coord the rollout. Note: autoscaler observed lower inflight count due to enforcement dropping requests, so it didn't scale up which amplified latency. We'll investigate autoscaler inputs too.
mike_eng_infra: Agree. Also checking autoscaler triggers: it currently uses successful request/throughput to decide scale, not queued/blocked requests. That made the situation worse when enforcement cut traffic. We'll add a ticket to incorporate queue depth/failed requests as scaling signals.
anna_support: Customer asked ETA. cc @luis_custsuccess for comms.
luis_custsuccess: I'll send an interim message: "We identified a quota unit mismatch causing throttles; applying temporary cap and unit fix now. Will follow with full timeline."
jess_sre: Running: `rwctl tenant update t-acme-9 --quota-unit tokens_per_minute --quota 100000`
deploy-bot: deploy started for tenant-config-rollout-20231102 by jess_sre (rollout id r-9944)
mike_eng_infra: Watching enforcement: reconcile applied on 4/4 nodes, enforcement caches invalidated. Queue depth dropped within ~60s and 429 rate fell immediately.
anna_support: Customer reports 429s mostly cleared within 2 minutes, a few lingering while caches warmed. They confirmed traffic returning to normal.
jess_sre: Added immediate alert rule: emit if tenant.metadata.quota_unit != expected_unit, priority=high. Creating INF-4523 to add validation for CLI/CSV migrations and a migration checker in tenant-import path.
ravi_product: Also adding UX change to tenant page to surface quota unit and show a tooltip about request vs token semantics for common model families.
luis_custsuccess: Sent customer update and asked them to confirm stability. They acked: "Thanks, looks good now." :white_check_mark:
anna_support: Summary for records: root cause = migration/ingest changed quota unit from tokens_per_minute to requests_per_minute -> enforcement applied request-limited bucket -> token-heavy workload triggered 429s. Remediation = updated tenant quota unit to tokens_per_minute + temporary quota increase, rolled config, added alerts + migration guard + UI surface. Please add postmortem and follow-up tickets.
jess_sre: Created postmortem stub: /ops/postmortems/2023-11-02-acme-quota-unit-mismatch and linked INF-4523.
mike_eng_infra: Filed autoscaler-signal ticket: INF-4530 to consider queue depth and rejected_requests as scale signals.
anna_support: Thanks everyone. Closing thread once postmortem is filled. :thumbsup:
